ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, proposed managers and authorized signatories against (i) the French national asset-freeze list (Liste unique de gel des avoirs — DG Trésor), (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (EU-CONSIL), (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists, (iv) the US OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists applicable to USD wire transactions, and (v) Interpol notices and adverse-media databases. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) identification and enhanced due diligence are required under Article L. 561-10 of the Code monétaire et financier for foreign PEPs, members of international organizations, and domestic PEPs where designated. Beneficial owners must be identified through each ownership layer above the 25% threshold or control otherwise exercised by any means; the French RBE declaration must be filed at incorporation and kept current within 30 days of any change. The screening protocol must be documented and retained for five years, and any hit or suspicion must be escalated to Tracfin (French FIU) under Article L. 561-15 of the Code monétaire et financier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI (https://guichet-entreprises.inpi.fr), with company registry data and availability checks through the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) accessible via Infogreffe and data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written using Latin alphabet characters and be capable of French transliteration/transcription; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated and a French-language version must appear in the articles of association and RCS filing. The name must include the legal form indicator 'SAS' or the full form 'Société par actions simplifiée'. The name must be lawful, distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to public policy or bonnes mœurs, and must not create a likelihood of confusion with pre-existing RCS-registered names or French/EU trademarks in the same field of activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory pre-incorporation name reservation system; name protection attaches only upon successful RCS registration. Availability is verified against the RCS, EUIPO and INPI trademark databases at the time of filing through the Guichet unique. If the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce or the INPI rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a reasoned rejection notification via the Guichet unique. The constitutional counsel may (i) file written observations before the Director of the INPI within two months of the rejection notice, invoking distinctive character and absence of confusion under Article L. 711-3 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle; (ii) file a summary application (référé) before the President of the commercial court or the Tribunal judiciaire to compel the registry to proceed; or (iii) immediately file a modified name application to avoid operational delay. Where rejection is based on a third-party trademark, the applicant may obtain a written coexistence consent letter or initiate invalidation proceedings in court. Final judicial appeal lies to the Cour d'appel within one month of the first-instance decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a transitional domiciliation arrangement under Article L. 123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code for a maximum period of five years from incorporation, subject to the domiciliation provider being licensed under Article R. 123-167. For an industrial EV bus OEM, a virtual office alone is commercially and regulatorily inadequate: the company must establish a physical industrial establishment and genuine administrative premises in France to meet the siège réel doctrine and to obtain the necessary ICPE environmental authorization and manufacturing license; reliance solely on a virtual office would heighten tax-residence and anti-abuse challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high for the EV bus manufacturing industry: unannounced on-site inspections by DREAL (ICPE environmental enforcement) and tax audits by DGFiP/URSSAF carry approximately a 60-70% probability within the first 24 months of commencement of industrial operations; at the pre-incorporation stage, physical inspection risk is low (approximately 5-10%) and limited to verification of the domiciliation address and UBO documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VI — Articles L.227-1 to L.227-27 (Société par Actions Simplifiée) and Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general incorporation rules); RCS registration governed by Articles L.123-1 and R.123-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office district; filing is processed through the single business formalities portal (Guichet Unique) operated on behalf of the RCS by the French National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-creation declaration (Déclaration de création d'entreprise, reference M0) completed on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and lodged with the notarised or signed original Articles of Association and all statutory annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A French SAS has no statutory minimum share capital; the capital is freely fixed by the Articles. However, the capital must be fully subscribed, and at least 50% of cash contributions must be paid up before registration and held in a blocked capital account (compte de dépôt bloqué) at a licensed French bank or before a notary; the balance must be paid within five years. In-kind contributions must be fully delivered, and the President must certify the deposit for release no earlier than the issue of the RCS registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Our written decision records the following unanimous resolutions of the founding shareholders: (1) The subscription and allocation of the entire share capital is ratified in all respects; the President is directed to certify the escrowed capital release once the French registration certificate (extrait Kbis) is issued. (2) The registered office is adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Association, and the President is authorised to file the registration application with the competent commercial court registry. (3) [Name] is hereby appointed President of the Société par Actions Simplifiée, with full authority to represent the Company, open bank accounts, execute lease agreements, engage employees and obtain all industrial, environmental and operating permits for the electric bus manufacturing facility.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles and escrowing of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The founding shareholders; a licensed French bank or a notary of the registered-office department (blocked capital account); no petition to the RCS is needed at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the written Articles of Association of the SAS (corporate name, corporate form, registered office, corporate object, share capital, allocation of shares, rules of direction and decision-making, appointment of the first President). Open a blocked capital account in the proposed corporate name, transfer at least 50% of cash contributions, and obtain the bank's attestation de blocage des fonds; have the bank state that the funds will be released only upon presentation of the Kbis registration certificate. Collate the identity, address and declaration of no bankruptcy/disablement of the President and shareholders.
required_dossiers: Original executed statuts (Articles of Association) including signature pages of all shareholders
Founders' identification documents (valid passport or national ID and proof of residential address)
Bank certificate of blocked capital deposit (attestation de blocage des fonds)
Domiciliation agreement or property-ownership title covering the registered office
Declaration of the designated President confirming the absence of judicial disqualification or personal bankruptcy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or notary rejects the capital certificate because of an irregularity, correct the wiring/origin-of-funds documentation and re-issue the attestation; if the Articles contain contested clauses, amend statutory language by a supplementary written act signed by all shareholders before any filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the corporate incorporation notice in a legal gazette (annonce légale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An approved Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) licensed in the department where the registered office is seated.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and place the public notice containing the corporate form 'SAS', corporate name, corporate object, registered office address, amount and division of share capital, corporate duration, the identity of the President, and the seat of the RCS where registration is sought. Obtain the certificate of publication (attestation de parution) and a copy of the published notice; these must accompany the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Completed annonce légale text per the statutory template
Copy of the executed statuts to validate the disclosure data
Blocked-capital certificate to state the paid-up amount when the notice mentions capital releases
Identity and powers of the first President for the officer disclosure section
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice because it diverges from the statuts or lacks a mandatory mention, revise the notice and republish; an incorrect or incomplete annonce légale is cured by a new publication and the corrected attestation is resubmitted with the registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation application with the Single Business Formalities Portal (Guichet Unique)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); the dossier is transferred electronically to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE, the URSSAF and tax authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 electronic declaration, attach the executed statuts, the legal publication certificate, the bank blocked-deposit certificate, the registered-office domiciliation agreement, the acceptance-of-office forms, the beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), any manager personal-specimen files, and pay the registration and public-legality fees online. The Greffe verifies legal offer compliance; after approval, the file is transmitted to the other authorities.
required_dossiers: Executed original Articles of Association
Attestation of publication in the legal gazette (JAL)
Attestation de blocage des fonds from the bank or notarial escrow
Domiciliation agreement or title/lease of the registered office
Declaration of beneficial owners (art. L.561-45-1 Code monétaire et financier)
Acceptance of office of the President and any undersigned directors
Certificate of no criminal/economic disqualification for management
Identity documents and required KYC data for the filing parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues an injunction to regularise (demande de pièces complémentaires), cure the identified defects within the statutory grace period (generally 15 days or 30 days as notified); on persistent refusal, seek a decision from the President of the Commercial Court in chambers (référé) under the Code of Commerce, or withdraw and amend the statutory file before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS entry and issuance of the Kbis registration certificate, SIREN/SIRET and EU VAT number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) and INSEE / French tax authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the dossier, the Greffe registers the company on the RCS, returns the legal-journal and letters, data-marks the SIREN and SIRET business identifiers and the intra-community VAT number; the company obtains the extract Kbis (uniquely). The President must confirm the release of the blocked capital using the certificate and arrange for the corporate bank operating account to be activated.
required_dossiers: Proof of submission of the full Guichet Unique file (recepisse de dépôt)
Payment receipt for greffe costs and legal-publicity duties
Statement of the registered-office address and officer appointments as entered in the application
Beneficial-ownership declaration receipt generated by the portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis extract reflects defective data (address, object, officers), file a rectification or mention in a formal petition with the Greffe; if the VAT number or SIREN is delayed or mismatched, contact the INSEE hotline and obtain the attestation of identification; appeal from any refusal to the Commercial Court within the applicable legal time-limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration corporate governance and employer status formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The Société's management bodies and, for employer formalities, URSSAF, the occupational-health service and the mutual/B2B insurance pools.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first formal meeting or written decision of the shareholders/board to ratify the choice of banking establishment, corporate seal, distribution of powers and adoption of internal accounting, authorisation and compliance registers. The company must complete the URSSAF employer registration (employer account), join an accredited occupational-health service (service de santé au travail interentreprises), and contract civil liability/worker compensation and vehicle-product insurance consistent with the bus-manufacturing exposure.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written decisions of the first shareholders/board meeting
Kbis certificate and SIREN/SIRET/VAT identification documents
Corporate bank account confirmation (RIB) for the domestic transit or supplier payment it may use for SWIFT wires
URSSAF employer registration form and the occupational-health affiliation agreement
Evidence of property/casualty and vehicle assembly/professional-indemnity insurance coverage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or the health service refuses affiliation because of an erroneous activity code, rectify the NAF/APE code attributed by INSEE and resubmit; any defect in authorisation procedures is cured by a new decision of the shareholders' meeting retroactive-registered in the company's register of decisions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and the department Prefecture acting for the Ministry for Ecological Transition, for ICPE installations; UTAC CERAM for vehicle manufacturer type-approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation préfectorale d'exploiter une Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) for the bus manufacturing, painting and battery-storage facility, together with the industrial vehicle national type-approval certificate (réception CE) where the buses are homologated as complete vehicles.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion — General Direction for Risk Prevention (DGPR), delivered through the DREAL and the department Prefecture.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA (évaluation environnementale systématique) is required where the plant falls under the ICPE authorisation regime and the relevant nomenclature headings listed in the Annex to Article R.122-2 of the Environment Code; facilities classified only at registration level may proceed with a simplified 'enregistrement' dossier combining an environmental notice and implementation conditions. An Exempt status is not available for an EV bus OEM with painting and lithium-battery storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Directive 2010/75/EU as transposed: wastewater after treatment must meet the general ICPE discharge limits (pH 5.5-8.5, TSS ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 120 mg/L, hydrocarbons ≤ 10 mg/L, heavy metals per Arrêté ministériel of 02/02/1998); coating/solvent installations must apply VOC control and where annual solvent consumption exceeds 150 t, an abatement efficiency of at least 90% (IED Art. 59 et seq.); storage of lithium-ion cells/packs must comply with ICPE battery-storage safety distances, passive fire-protection and dedicated retention basins; end-of-life bus batteries must be processed through approved take-back and recycling channels under EU Regulation 2023/1542, with waste records retained under the Environment Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance: commission-de-sécurité visit by SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours) and issue of the fire conformity certificate for the industrial building, escape routes and extinguishing systems. Structural clearance: static and dynamic structural-load inspection of roofing, gantry cranes, bus lifts and assembly mezzanines by an accredited technical-control organisation (APAVE, Bureau Veritas or Dekra) under the French building and Labour Code. Occupational clearance: CARSAT and Labour Inspectorate compliance for noise, vibration, electrical and machine-safety risk prevention, including the mandatory occupational-health enrolment, PPE plans and emergency-response drills before production start.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS entities obtain SIREN and SIRET numbers automatically upon registration with the Chambre des Métiers et de l'Artisanat. Non-resident foreign-owned entities must register on impots.gouv.fr to secure a French tax identification number (TIN) and intra-EU VAT ID, submitting incorporation certificate, articles of association, proof of address, and beneficial ownership details.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under French law. Corporate taxation applies at the entity level with no elective treatment for hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for all B2B transactions through the French eFacture platform, requiring real-time data transmission to tax authorities and issuance of compliant electronic invoices with digital fiscal stamps for clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods exported outside the EU upon proof that the goods have left EU territory. Offshore services supplied to non-EU customers qualify for 0% VAT with evidence of performance outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU), Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of export zero-rating trigger penalties of up to 40% of evaded VAT plus interest and possible criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment. Retrospective clawback applies if export documentation is absent or insufficient.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), acting within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank; capital-movement and FDI policy implemented by the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor, French Treasury); prudential and AML supervision by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility as an EU member under Articles 63-65 TFEU; euro flows are entirely unrestricted for share capital, dividends, royalties, debt service, and liquidation proceeds. The only gateways on profit remittance are corporate distributability rules and tax withholding at source (25% French statutory WHT; 0% intra-EEA under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive; 5-10% under the France-China DTA). The sole non-FX screening step is the FDI prior-authorisation regime (CMF Articles L151-1 et seq. and Decree No. 2019-1590) for non-EEA investors in listed sensitive sectors; electric-bus assembly is presumptively non-sensitive unless dual-use or critical-technology components are involved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline applies to French export proceeds. Export revenues may be freely retained in EUR or any foreign currency, converted at the company's discretion via standard bank FX products, and remitted to any counterparty. The only obligation is statistical cross-border payment/collection reporting transmitted by the bank to Banque de France for balance-of-payments compilation, which does not restrict liquidity or require prior approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre/bloqué) for initial share capital; Operational EUR current account with trade-finance and LC desk
Operational EUR current account plus import documentary credit (LC) and Surety Bond facility
Operational EUR account with linked USD/CNH multicurrency accounts and cross-border cash-concentration services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate & Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole CIB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR current account with green-transition financing framework for electric-vehicle manufacturers

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: CIC / Groupe Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR current account with SEPA public-sector collection services
Operational EUR account limited to domestic low-velocity transactions; unsuitable for LC/trade finance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for core treasury, Medium as an ancillary low-value disbursement rail. An offshore non-EEA digital EMI cannot lawfully provide the documentary-credit, guarantee, or public-sector settlement services required by an electric-bus OEM without full credit-institution licensing and a French/EEA passport; reverse-solicitation use is tolerable only for small operating expenses and must be swept daily to the Tier-1 bank. An EEA-licensed EMI (e.g., Wise Europe or Revolut) may automate expense payments but must not become a repository for municipal LC proceeds or import-settlement balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French Tier-1 banks generally mandate an in-person KYC interview of the SAS legal representative and each material UBO at a French branch, or an authentication before a notary with apostilled powers of attorney; fully remote opening is reserved for low-risk single-shareholder structures on digital banking platforms. The practical minimum is: apostilled board resolution appointing signatories, passport copies for all signatories/UBOs, INPI UBO declaration, registered-office proof, and at least one physically present signatory - alternatively a locally mandated director (directeur délégué) with signature authority fully resolves the presence constraint.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA UBO with opaque intermediate holding chain and unexplained capital-contribution sourcing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: INPI beneficial-ownership declaration; notarised corporate tree; three years of audited financial statements of the entire UBO chain; bank reference letters; signed source-of-funds/net-worth statement; French counsel legal opinion confirming absence of bearer shares and criminal-proceeds exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Extreme revenue concentration on a few French municipal buyers combined with large APAC related-party imports
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed municipal contract files and procurement notices; Chorus Pro VAT/e-invoicing records; LC shipping sets (B/L, certificates of origin, DAU customs declarations); arm's-length TP dossier under Article L13 AA of the CGI; board-approved cash-flow forecast; sanctions screen of the full counterparty cascade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use / critical-technology components in battery management, inverters, or telematics triggering export-control diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Component-level dual-use screening matrix under Regulation (EU) 2021/821; end-use certificates of suppliers; EU general programme authorisation utilisation memo; denied-party and OFAC/EU sanctions screening reports; corporate export-compliance manual with attested responsible officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank hold on initial share-capital escrow pending formal incorporation of the SAS
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial or bank attestation of blocked deposit; signed draft statutes; application for registration with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; first board resolution on authorised signatories and banking mandate; post-registration Kbis certificate to release the funds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million and qualifying capital ownership. Research and development expenses may qualify for the French research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to qualification and documentation. Certain innovation, investment, regional-aid, and energy-transition incentives may apply only if specific statutory conditions are met. Tax holidays are not generally available to a standard metropolitan SAS solely because it manufactures electric buses.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. France does not impose a five-year time limit on ordinary corporate tax-loss carryforwards. Utilization is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million in the relevant year. Unused losses may generally be carried back to the immediately preceding financial year, subject to statutory limits and election requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, together with tax package forms 2058-A-SD through 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, 2050-SD through 2057-SD, and applicable supporting schedules, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account using the EFI or EDI procedure. Annual corporate tax instalments are paid electronically through the same professional account.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax instalments generally quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return and balance are generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For a financial year ending on another date, the return is generally due within three months after the year-end. The final balance is generally due by the filing deadline, subject to statutory payment rules. Corporate tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to exceptions for the first year, low liability, and short financial years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax identification details, financial year dates, activity, tax regime, and applicable tax-consolidation or group-election information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French permanent establishment or French subsidiary details. A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the French SAS as the taxpayer. Report the foreign parent only where the form specifically requires shareholder, group, consolidation, or related-party information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2050-SD to 2057-SD, balance sheet and profit-and-loss accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report French GAAP or permitted accounting-basis assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, purchases, payroll, depreciation, provisions, finance costs, foreign-exchange items, and accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses attributable to the French SAS. For a French permanent establishment, allocate profits using the authorized OECD approach and retain allocation evidence. Do not include foreign head-office amounts unless properly attributable to the French taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add non-deductible accounting expenses, taxable accounting income omitted from the accounts, and tax adjustments; deduct exempt income, non-taxable items, permitted deductions, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source items that are not legally attributable to the French entity or permanent establishment. Apply French limitation rules to interest, provisions, depreciation, entertainment, related-party expenses, and hybrid or anti-abuse items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report current-year tax losses, carried-forward losses used, losses carried back where elected, and remaining tax losses subject to the French annual utilization cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent cannot use the French SAS's losses merely through ownership. Losses must remain with the French taxpayer unless a valid French tax-consolidation regime or statutory restructuring rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-C-SD, allocation of taxable profit or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile taxable profit or loss, tax-consolidated allocations where applicable, and the amount transferred to Form 2065.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French entity's taxable result. Do not allocate profit to a foreign affiliate without arm's-length support, contractual evidence, and functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable capital gains, long-term gains, qualifying participation interests, depreciable asset disposals, and applicable exemptions or recapture adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French rules to disposals by the SAS. A non-resident shareholder's disposal of SAS shares is separately analyzed under French domestic law and the applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2059-E-SD, value added and workforce information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report turnover, value added, payroll and workforce data used for tax and statistical purposes and, where relevant, local business tax calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French operations and French employees. Foreign-group turnover or workforce is included only where the form or applicable tax requires it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter taxable profit, ordinary corporate income tax, reduced-rate profit where eligible, tax credits, instalments, withholding credits, balance payable, or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only where French law or an applicable treaty permits them and retain certificates of foreign tax paid. A foreign shareholder's tax residence does not create a credit in the SAS's return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report specified categories of non-deductible or specially disclosed expenses, including certain luxury, excessive, or non-business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose expenses paid to foreign related parties where the statutory disclosure criteria are met. Business purpose and arm's-length evidence should be retained in French or with reliable French translations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report related-party transactions, aggregate transaction categories, counterparties, and transfer-pricing information when the applicable threshold and filing conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including procurement, engineering, management fees, financing, guarantees, royalties, tooling, and intragroup sales of buses or components.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2258-SD, country-by-country reporting notification or report, where applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide country-by-country information or the identity and jurisdiction of the reporting entity for multinational groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated-revenue threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS may have notification obligations even when another group entity files the report. Confirm group revenue, reporting entity identity, filing jurisdiction, and exchange status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD, corporate income tax balance payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate and pay the final corporate income tax balance after crediting instalments and eligible credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through the French professional tax account. A foreign bank payment method should be validated in advance; late payment does not suspend interest or collection measures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% where the taxpayer fails to file within 30 days after a formal notice and potentially 80% in cases of fraudulent conduct or abuse of rights. Late payment generally attracts late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules, in addition to applicable surcharges. Understatements may attract 40% for deliberate conduct and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights. Electronic-filing failures may produce additional fixed or percentage-based penalties. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a penalty generally equal to the higher of 0.5% of the transactions concerned or 5% of the tax adjustments, subject to a minimum of EUR 10,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French SAS to a non-resident shareholder are generally subject to a 25% French withholding tax under domestic law, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or EEA parent may be exempt under the French parent-subsidiary regime, generally requiring a qualifying ownership percentage, minimum holding period, subject-to-tax status, and anti-abuse compliance. Dividends paid to French-resident corporate shareholders are generally not subject to withholding tax, although the participation-exemption regime may apply at shareholder level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Determine the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, entitlement to treaty benefits, minimum holding percentage, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test exposure, and applicable treaty article. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and collect beneficial-owner and anti-abuse evidence. Apply the reduced rate at source only where French administrative requirements and payer documentation procedures permit; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and seek a refund through the applicable French tax refund procedure. Maintain shareholder registers, board resolutions, payment records, residence certificates, treaty analyses, and evidence of entitlement. EU parent exemptions require specific French statutory forms and supporting declarations where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on many royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to the classification of the payment, the recipient's jurisdiction, domestic exemptions, and treaty relief. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to broad domestic withholding solely because it is interest, but exceptions apply, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, anti-abuse provisions, and special instruments. Treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to 0% to 10% and interest withholding to 0% to 10%, but rates must be verified under the specific treaty. EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief may apply where qualifying associated-company ownership, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and holding-period conditions are satisfied. Payments must also satisfy French deductibility, withholding, beneficial-owner, and anti-hybrid rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory full transfer-pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or belongs to a group meeting the statutory EUR 400 million threshold, subject to the detailed French rules. A French entity below that threshold must still be able to demonstrate arm's-length pricing and may be required to provide simplified documentation or information during an audit. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. The local file and master file thresholds and content must be checked against the law applicable for the relevant financial year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic-substance regulation equivalent to a dedicated ESR regime in certain other jurisdictions. Substance is enforced through the French abuse-of-law doctrine, general anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, principal-purpose-test treaty provisions, parent-subsidiary anti-abuse rules, and permanent-establishment principles. A French SAS should maintain real decision-making, qualified personnel, premises, operational assets, manufacturing capability, board governance, banking control, risk assumption, and contemporaneous commercial evidence. A conduit entity or intragroup financing or IP structure without genuine functions and risks may lose treaty or statutory benefits and may generate reassessment, withholding tax, penalties, and director exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating purchases, using false invoices, diverting company revenue, intentionally understating taxable profit, or maintaining parallel accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, and penalties up to 80% of the evaded tax. Criminal tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially reaching seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions and available aggravations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, personal tax-fraud liability, management bans, civil restitution, asset seizures, and professional disqualification. Travel restrictions may be imposed by judicial authorities where legally justified; imprisonment is possible following conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late filing, non-payment, and obstruction of tax audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 2065, failure to pay instalments or the final balance, ignoring formal notices, refusing legally required accounting access, or supplying incomplete records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Generally a 10% surcharge for late filing or payment, higher surcharges after formal notice or in cases of bad faith or fraud, and late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month. Obstruction may trigger additional assessments, procedural penalties, and criminal consequences in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur liability for serious and repeated non-payment or fraudulent conduct, including civil contribution to tax liabilities, management bans, asset-preservation measures, and criminal sanctions where obstruction or fraud is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpricing imported components, underpricing exported buses, non-arm's-length royalty or management fees, unsupported financing, guarantee fees, or allocation of French manufacturing profit to a low-substance foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment under the arm's-length principle, interest, penalties up to 40% for deliberate conduct or 80% for fraudulent conduct, and documentation penalties generally based on 0.5% of affected transactions or 5% of adjustments, subject to a EUR 10,000 minimum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for losses caused by deliberate mispricing or breach of tax duties, and criminal exposure where false records, fraud, corruption, or money laundering is involved.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty abuse, and beneficial-ownership failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit with no personnel, premises, decision-making, commercial risk, or beneficial ownership, or claiming treaty relief through a circular or artificial arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU exemption, withholding at the domestic rate, reassessment, interest, abuse-of-law penalties potentially up to 80%, and loss of deductions or tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil restitution and criminal liability where they knowingly implemented fraudulent structures. Courts may impose asset freezes, management prohibitions, and travel restrictions under applicable judicial procedures; imprisonment is possible for related fraud or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit distribution and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without distributable reserves, concealing losses, making distributions while insolvent, extracting shareholder loans, or transferring assets to foreign owners at undervalue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, shareholder and director liability, tax reassessment, insolvency clawback, and potential criminal sanctions for misuse of corporate assets or fraudulent bankruptcy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute to insolvency shortfalls, disqualified from management, held liable for misuse of company assets, and subjected to criminal penalties, including imprisonment where statutory elements are satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering, corruption, and sanctions breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using municipal procurement, letters of credit, agents, distributors, or foreign accounts to launder funds, pay bribes, conceal beneficial owners, evade sanctions, or falsify customs and trade documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines, confiscation, procurement exclusion, contract termination, tax reassessment, and imprisonment under the French Penal Code and applicable sanctions, anti-corruption, customs, and AML legislation. Corporate penalties may be substantially higher than individual fines and may include dissolution or prohibition from conducting activities in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers may be personally prosecuted for bribery, money laundering, sanctions evasion, customs fraud, or failure to prevent prohibited conduct. Possible consequences include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, management bans, civil restitution, and judicial travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, import VAT, and origin fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaring the customs value, tariff classification, origin, battery content, or importer of record for electric buses or components, or reclaiming import VAT without entitlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture of goods, late-payment interest, and criminal customs sanctions for deliberate fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs representatives may face joint or personal liability under applicable customs rules, criminal prosecution, asset seizure, and professional disqualification where intentional false declarations are proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Research tax credit and incentive abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming the research tax credit for routine engineering, unsupported prototype work, subcontractor costs without qualifying certification, duplicated expenditure, or expenditure not incurred by the French taxpayer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance and recovery of the credit, interest, and penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on negligence, bad faith, fraud, or abuse. False documentation may generate separate criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability to the company and criminal exposure for fraudulent claims, false records, or organized tax fraud; management bans and asset seizures may apply in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain accounting and beneficial-owner records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep reliable French accounting records, board minutes, shareholder registers, transfer-pricing evidence, ultimate beneficial-owner filings, contracts, or payment-support documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of deductions or tax positions, estimated assessment, accounting penalties, inability to defend treaty or tax-credit claims, and penalties for inaccurate or omitted beneficial-owner information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and directors may be personally liable for governance failures, civil damages, management bans, and criminal sanctions where concealment, false declarations, or money laundering is involved.
